market_holds: Spot $84.125 at the 2026-11-18 close, which is a 52-week low: down 14.2% over 5 sessions, down 19.9% over 20, and 55% below the 52-week high (sealed baseline). No usable implied move: the ATM legs were not two-sided. Skew was +1.3 vol points and put/call OI 0.9, both balanced. The baseline's deadband is 3.25% (one day at 51.6% realised vol). The five-day fall came with the sector, not with Futu news: HOOD fell from 84.58 to 68.29 (-19%) from 11-11 to 11-18, COIN 136 to 112, BTC about 74k to 63k, TIGR 4.02 to 3.66 (-9%), KWEB -8%, while QQQ was about -4% (Yahoo daily bars, own pull). Consensus Q3 revenue is about US$815M (about HK$6.39B, -11% QoQ) on Earnings Whispers' preview of 2026-11-11. Chartmill shows HK$6.89B and EPS of HK$23.09 per a search snippet. The bar is therefore uncertain, somewhere between -11% and -4% QoQ. There is no company guide. On 2026-08-20 management said quarter-to-date volume was 'down modestly sequentially', net new funded accounts were moderating and CAC was rising, and it kept the target of 800k net adds for 2026 (477k done in H1). The CSRC proposed penalty of RMB1.85B was booked in Q1, and the mainland wind-down is known. Short interest is about 3-9% of float depending on source. At roughly 140M ADS the market cap is about $11.8B, against a Q2 net-income run-rate of about US$1.87B annualised, so the shares trade at about 6x that run-rate. The price holds deep regulatory and activity pessimism.
view: The Q3 print is mostly a known quantity. Hong Kong cash ADT fell 12% QoQ (HKEX Q3, 2026-11-06). US retail equity volume rose: Robinhood's notional went from $956B in Q2 to $992B in Q3, +4%. Futu's mainland clients are sell-only. Management already flagged a modest sequential volume decline. Rebuilt from Q2's lines (commission HK$3.36B on HK$6.42T, interest HK$3.12B with rates firm after HKMA's 25bp hike on 2026-09-17, other HK$0.72B), a 12-20% volume decline gives revenue of about HK$6.5-6.8B. That beats the Earnings Whispers bar and is roughly in line with Chartmill's, so the headline probably lands neutral to slightly positive. What decides the 13:00 ET price is more likely the call at 07:30 ET: Q4-to-date activity, net asset flows and net adds against the 800k target. Those inputs are mixed to weak. HK ADT in October was HK$180.7B, about 30% below the Q3 run-rate. Futu's client assets were marked down by the HSI falling from 24,613 to about 23,300 and the Nasdaq from 26,861 to 25,437 between Sep 30 and late October. Crypto has crashed. Against that, early-November volatility usually lifts US retail turnover, which is most of Futu's volume. The stock already fell with HOOD and COIN this week, so some of the Q4 softness is in the price through the sector, but the move cannot be tied to anything Futu-specific. History argues against leaning on a beat: on 2025-05-29, 2026-05-28 and 2026-08-20 the open was 2.5-7.5% above the prior close and the stock gave much of that back by the close. Net: a slight lean up on the backward print and the valuation, offset by Q4 commentary and the tape. I cannot separate this from a coin flip with any confidence.

recommendation.reason: My arithmetic puts Q3 revenue at HK$6.5-6.8B, which beats the softer of two conflicting consensus figures and is in line with the other, so the backward print gives only a small lean. The line the stock likely trades on, Q4-to-date activity, net adds and asset flows, points weaker: Hong Kong October ADT was down about 30% against Q3, markets fell and crypto broke. I cannot show which side of that line the price sits on. The five-day fall tracks HOOD and COIN rather than Futu news, so it is not evidence about this release.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4-to-date comment that US trading volume and net asset inflows rose in October and November, together with a larger buyback, would make the 6x run-rate multiple bite and favour a long. A cut to the 800k net-add target or a new regulatory step (a final CSRC decision, Hong Kong restrictions) would favour a short.

self_critique: The case for up is stronger than 53 says. The stock is at about 6x run-rate earnings after a sector washout, the softer consensus implies a volume decline worse than the inputs suggest, US retail volume was a record, and Futu has a history of buybacks, so a clean beat with a buyback could add 5-10% to a deeply oversold name. The case for down: management already said in August that Q3 was softer, October Hong Kong turnover collapsed, client assets were marked lower, and Futu reactions have tended to fade by midday, so any opening gain could be gone by 13:00. Neither case outweighs the other, so I left p_up close to 50.
